'''Mike Titterington''' (1945–2023) was a Scottish statistician known for the breadth of his work. Perhaps best known for his work on [[mixture models]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Titterington |first1=D. M. |last2=Smith |first2=Adrian F. M. |last3=Makov |first3=U. E. |title=Statistical analysis of finite mixture distributions |date=1995 |publisher=Wiley |location=Chichester |isbn=9780471907633 |edition=Reprint |url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/statistical-analysis-of-finite-mixture-distributions/oclc/11972604 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> and [[neural network]]s,<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Kay |editor1-first=J. W. |editor2-last=Titterington |editor2-first=D. M. |title=Statistics and neural networks: advances at the interface |date=1999 |publisher=Oxford Univ. Press |location=Oxford |isbn=9780198524229 |edition=1. publ |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/52996 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> he also published in [[optimal design]], [[smoothing]] techniques, [[image analysis]], [[spatial statistics]] and [[hidden Markov model]]s.<ref name="rssnews-obit" />

Titterington was educated at the [[High School of Stirling]] before going on to the University of Edinburgh (obtaining a [[British undergraduate degree classification#First-class honours|first class degree]]) then a Diploma in Mathematical Statistics (with distinction) from the University of Cambridge.<ref name="jrssa">{{cite journal |last1=Bowman |first1=Adrian |title=Donald Michael Titterington, 1945–2023 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society |date=22 December 2023 |volume=186 |issue=4 |pages=894–895 |doi=10.1093/jrsssa/qnad074}}</ref> Under [[Peter Whittle (mathematician)|Peter Whittle]] at Cambridge he continued to study for a PhD on stochastic nonlinear control.<ref name="mathgene"/>

Post-PhD, Titterington spent his entire career working at the Department of Statistics at the University of Glasgow: first research assistant, then lecturer. He was appointed as a professor in 1982 and chair of statistics in 1988 before retiring in 2011.<ref name="ims-obit">{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Peter J |last2=Robert |first2=Christian P |author2-link=Christian Robert |title=Obituary: D.M. Titterington 1945–2023 |url=https://imstat.org/2023/07/16/obituary-d-m-titterington-1945-2023/ |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |access-date=22 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> During this time he was editor of several statistics journals, including the [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society#Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Statistical Methodology)|Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B]] (1986–89) and [[Biometrika]] (1996–2007).<ref>{{cite web |title=In remembrance |url=https://academic.oup.com/biomet/pages/in-remembrance |website=Biometrika |publisher=Oxford Academic |access-date=22 June 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He edited (with [[David Cox (statistician)|David Cox]]) "Biometrika: One Hundred Years", collecting notable papers from the journal.<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Titterington |editor1-first=D. M. |editor2-last=Cox |editor2-first=D. R. |editor2-link=David Cox (statistician) |title=Biometrika: One Hundred Years |date=2001 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford New York |isbn=9780198509936 |edition=1. |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/54494 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> He also was involved in the [[Royal Statistical Society]] (roles including honorary secretary and chair of the research section and vice president).

The Guy Medal in Silver was awarded to Titterington in 2006 for his 1981 paper<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Titterington |first1=D. M. |last2=Murray |first2=G. D. |last3=Murray |first3=L. S. |last4=Spiegelhalter |first4=D. J. |author4-link=David Spiegelhalter |last5=Skene |first5=A. M. |last6=Habbema |first6=J. D. F. |last7=Gelpke |first7=G. J. |title=Comparison of Discrimination Techniques Applied to a Complex Data Set of Head Injured Patients |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series A (General) |date=1981 |volume=144 |issue=2 |pages=145 |doi=10.2307/2981918 |jstor=2981918 }}</ref> on discrimination methods and "for his important contributions to many areas of statistics, including the analysis of mixtures, incomplete data, latent structure analysis, neural networks, pattern recognition and machine learning, statistical smoothing, medical statistics and the design of experiments."<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Holt |first1=Tim |author1-link=Tim Holt |title=Report of the Council for the Session 2005–2006 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society |date=1 October 2006 |volume=169 |issue=4 |pages=913–1002 |doi=10.1111/j.1467-985X.2006.00445.x }}</ref>

He was a good friend of [[Peter Gavin Hall|Peter Hall]], for whom he wrote an obituary in the Royal Statistical Society and [[American Statistical Association]] magazine [[Significance (magazine)|Significance]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Titterington |first1=Mike |title=Remembering Peter Gavin Hall |journal=Significance |date=1 April 2016 |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=48 |doi=10.1111/j.1740-9713.2016.00905.x |access-date=22 June 2025 |url=https://academic.oup.com/jrssig/article/13/2/48/7029134}}</ref> The pair authored 21 papers together.<ref>{{cite web |title=MathSciNet Search |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/publications-search?query=auid%3A190188%20auid%3A172880 |website=MathSciNet |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref>

Titterington died in April 2023 after having been affected for many years by [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref name="ims-obit" />

==Honours==

* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in (1986)
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (1991)<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Donald Titterington |url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-donald-titterington-227/ |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref>
* Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] (1991)<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Members |url=https://isi-web.org/our-members?title=T&alphabet=A&view=in_memoriam#scroll-to-form |website=International Statistical Institute |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref>
* Royal Statistical Society Guy Medal in Silver (2006)<ref name=":0" />
* Mahalanobis Lecturer by the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] (2007)<ref name="jrssa"/>
